extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students, and review teams planning or conducting systematic reviews or scoping reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting a systematic- or scoping-review protocol that documents planned methods and for registering/publishing that protocol. Covers required protocol contents, registration options (PROSPERO, OSF, Figshare), and available templates/resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for the review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The protocol should explain why the review is being done — the purpose and justification that motivates the research question and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key questions structured (PICO or other)
rubrics_metrics.description: key questions broken into PICO (or other structured research question) components
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the review's main questions using a structured format such as PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) or another appropriate structure to make eligibility and search strategies explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify detailed eligibility criteria (study designs, populations, settings, timeframes, languages, outcomes, etc.) so selection decisions are reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search strategy (published and unpublished)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the search methods and sources (databases, grey literature, registries, handsearching) and how unpublished or non‑peer‑reviewed evidence will be sought and handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data abstraction and data management
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline the data extraction/processes, forms or tools to be used, who will perform extraction, procedures for resolving disagreements, and plans for data storage and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of methodological quality / risk of bias of individual studies
rubrics_metrics.description: assessment of methodological quality/risk of bias of individual studies (not required for scoping reviews)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which risk-of-bias or quality appraisal tools will be used and how assessments will be conducted and incorporated into synthesis. Note: scoping review protocols may not require this element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data synthesis methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned methods for synthesizing data (qualitative synthesis, meta-analysis, subgroup or sensitivity analyses), criteria for pooling studies, and how heterogeneity will be assessed and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading the evidence for each key question
rubrics_metrics.description: grading the evidence for each key question
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for assessing the overall certainty/strength of evidence for each key question (e.g., GRADE) and how that grading will be performed and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol as a planning document and roadmap
rubrics_metrics.description: A protocol is your planning document and roadmap for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that the protocol improves efficiency and accuracy, facilitates team understanding, and makes manuscript writing easier; journals and reporting standards increasingly expect registered protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register the protocol with an appropriate registry
rubrics_metrics.description: After you write the protocol, you should register it with a review registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register key protocol features in a registry (e.g., PROSPERO, OSF) to create a permanent, time-stamped record that enables comparison between planned and reported methods/outcomes. Registration is generally free and open to anyone undertaking systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose registry appropriate to review type (PROSPERO vs OSF/Figshare)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are numerous review registries available, such as PROSPERO or OSF. NOTE: Scoping reviews may not be registered with PROSPERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PROSPERO for prospective systematic reviews in health/social care where eligible; for scoping reviews and some other review types, use OSF or Figshare. Verify registry scope and eligibility before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSF pre-registration specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF can be used to pre-register a systematic or scoping review protocol and to share documents such as a citation management library, search strategies, and data extraction forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSF does not perform editorial review prior to registration — teams create their own pre-registration and can upload related documents. Use OSF when editorial registration review is not required or when you want to share underlying materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol publication options and journal policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocols may be eligible for publication in certain journals in certain disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some journals publish protocols (e.g., BioMed Central Protocols, BMJ Open, JBI Evidence Synthesis, Systematic Reviews). Check journal policies: some accept protocols without peer review if there is formal ethical approval and recognized funding; others subject protocols to peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established templates and reporting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of PRISMA-P, PROSPERO template, JBI scoping review protocol template, Generalized Systematic Review Registration Form, Evidence Synthesis Protocol Template, and standards (Institute of Medicine, Cochrane Handbook, JBI Manual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow recognized templates and reporting standards (PRISMA-P, Cochrane, IOM, JBI) to ensure the protocol contains essential elements; these resources include checklists and explanations for what to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROSPERO records key protocol features and provides public permanent record
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPERO is an international database of prospectively registered systematic reviews in health and social care. Key features from the review protocol are recorded and maintained as a permanent record in PROSPERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registering with PROSPERO enables comprehensive listing of reviews registered at inception and facilitates comparison of reported findings with planned methods; consult 'How to register with PROSPERO' for submission steps and eligibility.
